A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 37-page CounselBench paper, including Appendices A–I. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks establish complete comparability; differences are confined to one reported percentage and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v3 reports original expert evaluations of counseling responses, results for 1,080 adversarial responses from nine LLMs, and additional empirical analyses in the appendices (Tables 1, 3–4 and 17–18).

after.justification: v4 retains the original expert-rating results, adversarial evaluations, LLM-judge comparisons and appendix experiments reported in v3.

M1.justification: The two-part benchmark construction, six evaluation dimensions, adversarial-question design and response-generation procedures are unchanged (Sections 3–5; Appendix D).

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100 CounselChat questions across 20 topics and 120 expert-authored adversarial questions. The appendix evaluations introduce no changed dataset, task or test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The response providers, human comparator and LLM-judge sets are identical within corresponding experiments. The MentalLLaMA and Meditron pilot comparisons in Appendix I are also retained unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H revises the reported share of human 'not sure' answers excluded from LLM–human agreement calculations from 0.09% to 0.9%. This changes the documented extent of evaluation-sample exclusion; the exclusion rule, metrics and other settings remain unchanged, and no rerun is established.

E4.justification: The annotator-time and experience analyses, sentence-level detection analysis, few-shot exploration and domain-specific model case studies are unchanged (Appendices C, D, H and I).

E5.justification: Statistical tests, standard-deviation reporting, seed information and three-sample averaging in Appendix H are unchanged. The revised 'not sure' percentage is a descriptive result, not a change to statistical uncertainty reporting practices.

E6.justification: The excluded-response percentage in Appendix H, page 35, changes from 0.09% to 0.9%. All other numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the judge scores in Table 4 and plotted results in Figure 8.

T1.justification: The rubric and scoring definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theoretical results, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain identical claims about clinically grounded benchmarking, recurring model failures and the shortcomings of LLM judges.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model-family failure patterns, LLM–human disagreement and limited few-shot benefits are unchanged. The discussion of data availability, applicability and challenges of extending evaluation to multi-turn dialogue is also identical.

D1.justification: Prompt templates, decoding parameters, data-selection and processing instructions, hardware, runtime information and code/data availability statements are unchanged. The exclusion rule itself is already documented identically in both versions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are identical, with no added citations or revised positioning relative to earlier benchmarks and adversarial evaluations.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v3 dated 4 March 2026 to v4 dated 14 May 2026. Apart from the numerical revision in Appendix H, wording, terminology, headings and section order are identical.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain identical displays, captions and placement. Rendered-page comparison shows no layout changes beyond the updated margin text and the shorter numerical token in Appendix H.

improvement.justification: v4 revises one reported exclusion percentage from 0.09% to 0.9% and updates the version/date stamp. The model comparisons, supporting analyses, conclusions and presentation otherwise remain identical. This isolated reporting revision does not establish a meaningful paper-level quality gain or loss.
